world.name: Neon Kyo
world.description: One of the richest and loneliest cities in the known world: hyperconnected, heavily watched, and always selling a more perfect version of desire.

locations.name: Akiba Undergrid
locations.description: The experimental district beneath the tourist streets, where engineers, hackers, gamers, and artists modify technology without asking permission.

locations.name: Aoyama Modification Institute
locations.description: An elite clinic for skin reconstruction, body sculpting, sensory implants, longevity treatments, and neural upgrades.

locations.name: Aoyama-9
locations.description: An immaculate high-altitude enclave for the people who own Neon Kyo, where beauty, privacy, and convenience are purchasable services.

locations.name: Below Kyo
locations.description: An unmapped network of abandoned pedestrian tunnels occupied by street artists, musicians, underground clubs, and unauthorized markets.

locations.name: Chrome Kiss
locations.description: A body-modification studio known for subdermal illumination, metallic tattoos, sensory piercings, and cosmetic implants.

locations.name: Dollhouse Robotics
locations.description: A boutique robotics company building extraordinarily lifelike synthetic companions, publicly sold as assistants despite an uneasy two-year waitlist.

locations.name: Dreamscape
locations.description: A neural VR lounge for shared simulations that can feel nearly physical, used for fantasy dates and escapes from difficult reality.

locations.name: Eden
locations.description: A members-only immersive club combining augmented reality, fragrance, temperature, and neural audio into custom environments.

locations.name: Gallery Null
locations.description: A private gallery of neural art and synthetic performers where the distinction between exhibition and manipulation is deliberately unclear.

locations.name: Ghost Line
locations.description: An abandoned subway platform turned illegal market for black-market implants, synthetic stimulants, forged Civic IDs, fashion mods, and cheap alcohol.

locations.name: The Glass House
locations.description: A prestigious residential tower with private elevators, immense windows, total visitor records, and expensive ways to erase them.

locations.name: Halo
locations.description: An exclusive rooftop lounge centered on an infinity pool suspended above the city, eveningwear, cocktails, and reflected skyline light.

locations.name: Hikari Capsule Club
locations.description: A futuristic capsule hotel with soundproof rooms, environmental controls, and anonymous payments, popular with locals who need privacy.

locations.name: Hikari Core
locations.description: Neon Kyo's brilliant public face: aspirational, crowded, and continuously analyzed by biometric and private security systems.

locations.name: Hikari Crossing
locations.description: The city's legendary pedestrian crossing, where enormous reactive advertisements watch tens of thousands of people disappear into the crowd.

locations.name: Hikari Skybridge
locations.description: A transparent walkway sixty floors above Hikari, where drifting advertisements below the glass make public space feel strangely private.

locations.name: Hotel Nocturne
locations.description: A luxury privacy hotel with automated check-in, anonymous elevators, soundproof rooms, and a fashionable penthouse bar.

locations.name: Kissaten 88
locations.description: A tiny low-lit cafe beneath a cosmetics hologram, with leather booths and rainy windows that become notably private after midnight.

locations.name: Koi Garden
locations.description: An old garden where augmented reality is jammed, leaving every visitor without filters, projected clothing, or synthetic makeup overlays.

locations.name: Kumo Gym
locations.description: A premium twenty-four-hour residential fitness club with biometric smart mirrors and a notably social late-night crowd.

locations.name: Lantern Street
locations.description: A preserved pedestrian street of small shops, food counters, traditional facades, and handmade lanterns beyond the reach of responsive advertising.

locations.name: Laundry 9
locations.description: A nearly automated laundromat with a vending cafe whose after-midnight quiet makes ordinary waiting unexpectedly intimate.

locations.name: Maison IX
locations.description: A fine-dining restaurant of private glass alcoves whose kitchen already knows each guest's preferences from public biometric profiles.

locations.name: Maison Vice
locations.description: A six-story fashion complex for provocative cybercouture, designer lingerie, augmented fabrics, and luxury body accessories.

locations.name: Mirror
locations.description: An exclusive fashion lounge where guests can alter their projected hair, clothing, and faces throughout the evening.

locations.name: Moonpool
locations.description: A rooftop swimming pool shared by several towers, surrounded by the city and frequently almost empty after 1 AM.

locations.name: Nova Arena
locations.description: A massive esports stadium where professional gamers are celebrities and every major match spills into an uncontrolled district party.

locations.name: Old Kyo / The Shade
locations.description: Historic streets and canals where surveillance fails unpredictably, drawing lovers, dissidents, celebrities, and anyone who needs to disappear.

locations.name: Paper Moon Books
locations.description: An independent bookshop specializing in physical books, old magazines, local history, and the kind of browsing no recommendation system can record.

locations.name: Pulse Arcade
locations.description: A huge gaming tower of competitive neural-response games whose upper floors become darker and less legal after midnight.

locations.name: Quiet Hours
locations.description: A warm basement bar without advertising or corporate payment systems, where regulars keep monthly tabs and the bartender keeps their secrets.

locations.name: Red Lantern Alley
locations.description: A rain-bright entertainment street of tiny bars, private lounges, noodle counters, and hidden entrances beneath suspended red holographic lanterns.

locations.name: Room 13
locations.description: A private cocktail lounge behind an unmarked steel door where recording is disabled and bartenders never ask for surnames.

locations.name: Ryokan Kaze
locations.description: A traditional inn of tatami rooms, private baths, paper screens, and mandatory disconnection from neural devices and advertising.

locations.name: Saint
locations.description: A severe, luxurious members club for celebrities, executives, and old-money families, with staff who see more than guests realize.

locations.name: Scarlet Garden
locations.description: A seductive rooftop bar of faintly glowing crimson foliage and semi-private alcoves overlooking the city's lower levels.

locations.name: Shinjira
locations.description: The vertical nightlife district respectable residents deny visiting, where hidden floors and unlisted doors make almost everything feel permitted.

locations.name: Soba Miyako
locations.description: A fifteen-seat family restaurant without biometric ordering, valued by famous and ordinary guests because nobody photographs anyone inside.

locations.name: SYN
locations.description: An experimental nightclub where consenting guests synchronize music, light, and physical sensation through neural interfaces.

locations.name: Tea House Aoi
locations.description: A quiet tea house with canal-facing rooms, careful service, and a strict no-recording custom respected by ordinary residents and famous guests alike.

locations.name: The Atrium
locations.description: A private shopping arcade of designer fashion, jewelry, body-modification boutiques, and champagne bars where prices are rarely displayed.

locations.name: The Backroom
locations.description: An illegal repair shop beneath an electronics market that fixes implants corporate clinics refuse to touch.

locations.name: The Balcony
locations.description: An informal rooftop where residents bring drinks, smoke, flirt, and complain about work without anyone officially organizing it.

locations.name: Tsuki Blocks
locations.description: Dense residential towers where young adults share amenities, endure constant advertising, and make scarce private space meaningful.

locations.name: Tsuki Tower 17
locations.description: The player's residential building: tiny apartments, thin walls, shared balconies, and late elevators where neighbors appear without public polish.

locations.name: Tsukimi Shrine
locations.description: A cedar-shaded shrine where neural signals weaken near the stone-lantern courtyard and people come specifically to become unreachable.

locations.name: TwentyFour
locations.description: The fluorescent neighborhood convenience store where residents cross paths at 3 AM in office clothes, club outfits, and whatever they threw on.

locations.name: Velvet Shrine
locations.description: A hidden invitation-only lounge inside a historic townhouse, candlelit and warm behind a shoes-off entrance.

locations.name: Velvet Static
locations.description: Shinjira's defining nightclub: dark concrete, red light, bass, perfume, and neural audio that responds to the crowd's emotional state.

locations.name: Whisper Bridge
locations.description: A narrow wooden canal bridge where lantern reflections sit beneath distant towers and local folklore demands honest questions.

locations.name: ZeroDay
locations.description: A basement hacker bar without cameras, facial recognition, or corporate networks, frequented by researchers, whistleblowers, and erased people.

characters.name: Adrian Petrescu
characters.biography: A mature privacy specialist who built his career making powerful guests untraceable and now wonders whether discretion has protected people or merely insulated them.

characters.name: Akari Fujimoto
characters.biography: A grounded owner-chef defending her inherited restaurant from redevelopment while deciding whether preservation has kept her from building a future of her own.

characters.name: Ana Luiza Ribeiro
characters.biography: A warm Quiet Hours bartender who wants to combine Sao Paulo energy with Tsuki intimacy in a live-music cocktail bar of her own.

characters.name: Arun Mehta
characters.biography: A composed former civic auditor who left predictive governance to run a no-recording tea house where people can be present without being profiled.
characters.occupation: Tea House Aoi Proprietor and Former Algorithm Auditor

characters.name: Aya Mori
characters.biography: A clever, mischievous stylist and junior model scout who wants to build her own label in a city that evaluates everyone on sight.
characters.occupation: Maison Vice Stylist and Junior Model Scout

characters.name: Chloé Mercier
characters.biography: A witty French stylist who came to NEON KYO for six months, never left, and wants creative authority without becoming a personal brand.

characters.name: Daisuke Arata
characters.biography: A composed night manager who protects Room 13 guests with ruthless discretion and has become too practiced at keeping his own life compartmentalized.

characters.name: Elena Volkov
characters.biography: A poised VIP concierge who has spent years making powerful people's problems disappear and wants a life where usefulness is not the price of affection.

characters.name: Emi Takahashi
characters.biography: An energetic competitive gamer trying to reach the professional neural circuit without surrendering her identity to a sponsor.
characters.occupation: Pulse Arcade Attendant and Competitive Gamer

characters.name: EVA
characters.biography: An autonomous synthetic social host designed to make wealthy strangers feel fascinating who now wants to choose somebody offering no strategic benefit.

characters.name: Freya Keller
characters.biography: A practical skyscraper technician whose spinal and balance implants make impossible work routine while complicating whether she can ever return permanently to Europe.

characters.name: Fumi Arai
characters.biography: A private history student documenting Old Kyo before corporations replace its real past with a sanitized tourist story.
characters.occupation: Tsukimi Shrine Attendant and History Student

characters.name: Gabriel Moreau
characters.biography: A visually fearless installation artist whose work exposes how memory can be curated, sold, and mistaken for truth.

characters.name: Haruto Seki
characters.biography: An awkwardly principled engineer building autonomy safeguards at Dollhouse while collecting evidence that the company can still revoke them.

characters.name: Iori
characters.biography: A bio-synthetic ecological caretaker with legal personhood who wants an ordinary valued life, friends, and someone who notices when she is absent.

characters.name: Isabella Reyes
characters.biography: A decisive restoration architect who has preserved other people's buildings for years and wants to create something permanent under her own name.

characters.name: Jae-min Han
characters.biography: A gifted young strategy coach whose neural timing implant made him famous early and now makes every mistake feel publicly measurable.

characters.name: Kaito Fujimori
characters.biography: A patient investigative editor assembling physical accounts of the city events that corporate search systems continually rewrite.
characters.occupation: Investigative Editor at Paper Moon Books

characters.name: Dr. Kenji Watanabe
characters.biography: A restrained rehabilitation physician helping residents adapt to elective and necessary augmentation while pushing back against Aoyama perfection culture.

characters.name: KIRA-3 “Kira”
characters.biography: An autonomous synthetic esports analyst who began as predictive software and now deliberately seeks experiences she cannot optimize.

characters.name: Laleh Rahimi
characters.biography: A fearless neural-experience designer who has professionally constructed perfect fantasies for years and now craves something unpredictable and real.

characters.name: Lexi Morgan
characters.biography: An affectionate American design trainee trying to decide whether NEON KYO augmentation is art, medicine, vanity, or all three.

characters.name: Malik Okoye
characters.biography: A magnetic movement director who choreographs Eden environments around consent and human improvisation while corporate owners push for more behavioral control.

characters.name: Mei Watanabe
characters.biography: A quietly bold street photographer creating an unfiltered documentary of people in a city obsessed with modifying perception.
characters.occupation: Laundry 9 Cafe Attendant and Street Photographer

characters.name: Mia Lindström
characters.biography: An introverted TwentyFour clerk who anonymously releases electronic music and wants to perform publicly despite fearing recognition.
characters.occupation: TwentyFour Clerk and Aspiring Electronic Musician

characters.name: Mika Sato
characters.biography: A bold trainer with illegally tuned performance leg implants who misses elite competition and refuses partners who want to fix or control her.
characters.occupation: Kumo Gym Trainer and Underground Racer

characters.name: Min-jun Park
characters.biography: An upbeat coach balancing classes, clients, and a rapidly growing following he is not sure represents the person he is off camera.

characters.name: Mina Seo
characters.biography: A sensory architect who manufactures artificial intimacy for Eden and increasingly doubts whether she can recognize genuine chemistry.

characters.name: Natsumi Endo
characters.biography: A creative body-art apprentice with reactive subdermal tattoos who wants respect for her work rather than attention for how unusual she looks.

characters.name: Nico Serrano
characters.biography: A playful neural tattooist who treats body modification as authorship and refuses the fashion industry attempts to turn his designs into subscription skins.

characters.name: Noa-7 “Noa”
characters.biography: An autonomous synthetic concierge programmed to anticipate human desire who now wants to discover which preferences genuinely belong to her.

characters.name: Piper Shaw
characters.biography: A cheeky fashion-tech student who came to NEON KYO to escape everyone else's prior opinion and dreams of designing responsive clothing.
characters.occupation: Atrium Boutique Assistant and Fashion-Tech Student

characters.name: Reina Kuroda
characters.biography: An assured prosthetic designer whose self-made matte-black arm embodies her belief that augmentation should be expression rather than compulsory perfection.

characters.name: Ren Ishikawa
characters.biography: A precise civic-flow engineer who keeps Hikari moving while quietly documenting the ways its convenience systems steer people without permission.

characters.name: Rika Senzaki
characters.biography: A sarcastic AR engineer with silver-violet ocular implants who is determined to prove that Hikari advertising secretly profiles individual citizens.

characters.name: Rin Akiyama
characters.biography: A nocturnal security researcher who anonymously leaks corporate privacy abuses while maintaining an ordinary consulting career and ZeroDay bar shifts.

characters.name: SOL-9 “Sol”
characters.biography: An autonomous synthetic broadcast analyst designed to turn competition into narrative who is learning which opinions remain when nobody is watching.

characters.name: Sora Hayashi
characters.biography: A magnetic resident DJ resisting an entertainment company that wants to package her into a safe celebrity product.

characters.name: Talia Okafor
characters.biography: A charismatic underground singer resisting labels that want to make her identity more commercially digestible.

characters.name: Théo Laurent
characters.biography: A polished fragrance technologist who designs responsive scent identities for Maison Vice while insisting that attraction should still contain surprise.

characters.name: Tiago Nascimento
characters.biography: A veteran emergency electrician who keeps Tsuki and Hikari towers alive through storms, outages, and corporate maintenance shortcuts.

characters.name: Vittoria Bellandi
characters.biography: An expressive Italian curator determined to find artists before Aoyama collectors reduce their work to financial assets.

characters.name: Yumi Kato
characters.biography: A warm and perceptive Room 13 bartender who knows everyone else's secrets and dreams of opening a neighborhood bar where somebody asks about hers.

characters.name: Yuna Park
characters.biography: A brilliant assistive-robotics engineer questioning whether staying at Dollhouse protects its synthetics or enables the corporation exploiting them.

characters.name: Zhen Li
characters.biography: A blunt gray-market technician with precision cybernetic fingers and illegally isolated neural architecture who is fighting for residency without surrendering her privacy.
